title: A follow-up has a bar to clear before it becomes a task
goal: Every task the loop finishes is asked to file whatever it left rough as a new task, and it does, faithfully. That is why the queue has grown by about forty tasks a week and now stands at sixty nine ready against a target of twelve. Most of them are real. Enough of them are near-twins of something already in the queue, or a wording nit nobody using the app would ever notice, that a request from the user lands behind a wall of the loop's own homework. Give a follow-up a bar to clear, and give the things that do not clear it somewhere to go that is not a new task.
notes:
Comes from the queue growth measured over the last seven days of queue/history.jsonl:
  2026-09-06 created 52 done 58 dropped 2
  2026-09-07 created 75 done 54 dropped 7
  2026-09-08 created 48 done 67 dropped 3
  2026-09-09 created 59 done 39 dropped 2
  2026-09-12 created 52 done 23 dropped 3
  2026-09-13 created 29 done 17 dropped 1
  totals: created 315, done 258, dropped 18
The 2026-09-13 07:14 manager report read a narrower window and concluded the queue was draining; over a week it is not, it grows about 40 a week. That report also predicted this exact fix ("if it is still above fifty in a week, the fix is a harder triage rule").

The instruction that produces the inflow is the acceptance line every feature task carries, "anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task", which comes from queue/bin/manager-prompt.md and is echoed in queue/bin/runner-prompt.md. The change belongs in runner-prompt.md (the bar and the fold-first rule), and the same wording wants to reach the digest and triage prompt so the three agree.

Deliberately NOT a cap on the number of follow-ups: a cap loses real findings silently. The bar plus a place to write the rest down keeps everything recoverable.

Evidence that near-twins are real, from today's queue: walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep names twelve failing walks, and six of the twelve already have their own diagnosed open task with its own reproduction (border-effect and glow-effect under adding-an-effect-leaves-every-one-of-its-setting, corner-radius-rounds under the-colour-popover-never-opens-in-the-corner-rad, dock-picked-first under picking-a-plain-shape-leaves-the-panel-parked-on, layers-lazy-rows under two-effect-walks-fail-now-and-then-because-a-pre, turn-into-a-picture under undo-in-a-walk-cannot-use-the-command-z-chord).
acceptance: The runner instructions say plainly what earns a follow-up task: something a person using the app would notice, that is not already covered by an open task
A rough edge that does not clear the bar is written into the finishing task's own log instead, so nothing is lost and the next pass can still find it
The instructions say to search the open queue and fold into the nearest existing task before filing a new one, and how to search
The same bar is written into whatever the digest and triage passes use, so three different passes do not each apply their own
Nothing in the change lets a runner skip filing a follow-up for something that is actually broken
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
